point: The subject receives the action: be + past participle.
主詞承受動作：be + p.p.
why: The badges do not hand anything out; they are handed out, and no object follows the blank. By the end of next week is future. So the answer is will be distributed.
識別證是被發放的一方，空格後沒有受詞；by the end of next week 是未來，所以用 will be distributed。

gloss.ex: Every visitor must wear a security badge.
Please send the report by the end of Friday.

point: rise takes no object; raise does.
rise 不接受詞；raise 要接受詞。
why: Nothing follows the blank except by nearly eight percent, so the verb has no object: costs rise on their own. Since the start of the year needs the present perfect: have risen.
空格後只有 by nearly eight percent，沒有受詞，運費自己上漲，用 rise；since the start of the year 配完成式：have risen。

gloss.ex: Shipping costs are shown at checkout.
Our overseas customers pay in local currency.

point: be granted + noun: the receiver is the subject.
be granted + 名詞：得到的人當主詞。
why: By the board of directors shows who gives the leave. Ms. Okafor receives it, so the verb is passive. A noun can still follow granted: a two-week paid sabbatical. The answer is was granted.
by the board of directors 表示給假的是董事會，Okafor 女士是接受者，用被動；granted 後面仍可接 a two-week paid sabbatical。答案是 was granted。

gloss.ex: She took a sabbatical to write a book.
The board of directors meets every quarter.
He got a bonus in recognition of his work.

point: The verb agrees with the subject, not the nearby noun.
動詞跟真正的主詞一致，不跟旁邊的名詞。
why: The subject is the plural projectors. In every conference room on the fourth floor only adds detail, so it does not change the verb. The answer is have.
主詞是複數的 projectors；in every conference room on the fourth floor 只是補充說明，不影響動詞。答案是 have。

gloss.ex: The projector in room two is broken.
Please book the conference room early.
We replaced the old printer with a new one.

point: A gerund subject takes a singular verb.
動名詞當主詞，動詞用單數。
why: The subject is the gerund Approving, not requests or customers. The act of approving is one thing, so the verb is singular: takes.
主詞是動名詞 Approving，不是 requests 或 customers。「核准這件事」是單數，所以用 takes。

gloss.ex: You can ask for a refund within a week.
Domestic flights are cheaper than overseas ones.

point: neither A nor B: the verb agrees with B.
neither A nor B：動詞跟 B 一致。
why: The noun closest to the blank is the two service contracts, which is plural. So the verb is plural: require.
離空格最近的名詞是 the two service contracts，是複數，所以動詞用複數：require。

gloss.ex: Please sign the lease agreement today.
The service contract covers repairs for two years.
The renewal date is June 1.

point: whose + noun: the noun belongs to the person before.
whose + 名詞：名詞屬於前面的人。
why: Subscriptions expire this month is already a full clause. The subscriptions belong to the customers, so the blank means 'their': whose.
subscriptions expire this month 已是完整子句；訂閱屬於 customers，空格相當於「他們的」，所以用 whose。

gloss.ex: My subscription ends in March.
The coupon will expire on Friday.
We sent a renewal reminder last week.

point: Preposition + relative pronoun: things take which.
介系詞 + 關係代名詞：事物用 which。
why: Two of points back to the five bids, which are things, not people. After the preposition of, things take which: two of which.
two of 指回前面的 the five bids，是事物不是人；介系詞 of 後面指事物用 which：two of which。

gloss.ex: We received three bids for the contract.
The renovation will take two months.
The project finished under budget.

point: The missing object is a thing: which.
缺的受詞是事物：用 which。
why: Brenvale Foods acquired has no object. The missing object is The Dunmore plant, which is a thing. After the comma, the word is which.
Brenvale Foods acquired 後面沒有受詞；缺的正是 The Dunmore plant，是事物。逗號後用 which。

gloss.ex: The plant employs about two hundred people.
The firm acquired a smaller rival.
We changed our packaging to save money.

point: A possessive goes before a noun: its.
所有格放在名詞前：its。
why: Return policy is a noun, so the blank needs a possessive. Venlow Logistics is one company, so the word is its.
return policy 是名詞，空格要用所有格；Venlow Logistics 是單數的公司，所以用 its。

gloss.ex: Our return policy is posted on the website.
We accept exchanges within two weeks.

point: those of stands for a plural noun already named.
those of 代替前面已出現的複數名詞。
why: The sentence compares delivery times with the delivery times of competitors. To avoid saying a plural noun twice, use those: those of its main competitors.
句子比的是運送時間和競爭對手的運送時間。為了不重複複數名詞，用 those：those of its main competitors。

gloss.ex: Our delivery times are now much shorter.
Prices rose considerably last year.
Our main competitor lowered its prices.

point: A possessive pronoun stands alone for 'my + noun': mine.
所有代名詞單獨使用，代替「我的 + 名詞」：mine。
why: The verb took comes right after the blank, so the blank is the subject and has no noun after it. It means 'my request', so the word is mine.
took 緊接在空格後面，空格是主詞，後面沒有名詞；意思是「我的申請」，所以用 mine。

gloss.ex: Reimbursement usually takes ten days.
Please keep the receipt for your records.

point: decide + to + verb.
decide 後面接 to + 動詞。
why: The verb decided is followed by to + verb, not an -ing form. So the answer is to postpone.
decided 後面接 to + 動詞，不接 -ing。所以答案是 to postpone。

gloss.ex: The bank opened a new branch downtown.
The renovation will take two months.

point: in addition to: to is a preposition, so use -ing.
in addition to 的 to 是介系詞，後面接 -ing。
why: In in addition to, the word to is a preposition. A verb after a preposition takes -ing: editing the monthly newsletter.
in addition to 的 to 是介系詞，介系詞後面的動詞用 -ing：editing the monthly newsletter。

gloss.ex: In addition to salary, we offer training.
Our newsletter goes out every month.
She manages a team of six people.

point: let + object + base verb.
let + 受詞 + 原形動詞。
why: Let is followed by an object and a base verb, without to. After the two new technicians, the verb is carry out.
let 後面接受詞加原形動詞，不加 to。在 the two new technicians 後面，動詞用 carry out。

gloss.ex: A technician will visit the office today.
The server upgrade is planned for Sunday.
They solved it on their own.

point: than needs a comparative.
than 前面要用比較級。
why: Than follows the blank, so use a comparative adjective. Much only makes it stronger: much cheaper.
空格後面有 than，要用比較級形容詞；much 只是加強語氣：much cheaper。

gloss.ex: Shipping takes three days.
The goods travel by rail to the port.

point: the + comparative, the + comparative.
the + 比較級, the + 比較級。
why: The earlier starts a pair, so the second half needs the + comparative: the more guests. The earlier the invitations are sent, the more guests are likely to come.
The earlier 開啟對應句型，後半句要用 the + 比較級：the more guests。意思是邀請函寄得越早，可能來的人越多。

gloss.ex: We mailed the invitations on Monday.
We will send out the notices today.
The product launch is in May.

point: superior is followed by to.
superior 後面接 to。
why: Superior already means 'better', so it takes to, not than: superior to that of every competing model.
superior 本身就有「比較好」的意思，後面接 to，不接 than：superior to that of every competing model。

gloss.ex: This phone has a long battery life.
Customers rated the service as excellent.
We compared three competing products.

point: Uncountable noun: use much.
不可數名詞：用 much。
why: Information is uncountable. It has no plural form, so it takes much: not … much information.
information 是不可數名詞，沒有複數形，所以用 much：not … much information。

gloss.ex: The parking rules changed last month.
Ask the building management office about keys.

point: most of the + plural noun.
most of the + 複數名詞。
why: Of the applicants follows the blank, so the word must go before of the + a plural noun. Most does: most of the applicants means the larger part of them.
空格後面是 of the applicants，空格的字要能接 of the + 複數名詞。Most 可以：most of the applicants 是「大部分應徵者」。

gloss.ex: Each applicant sent a short resume.
She applied for a sales position.

point: Uncountable noun: a great deal of.
不可數名詞：a great deal of。
why: Equipment is uncountable, and the later words most of it treat it as one mass. So the quantity phrase must fit an uncountable noun: a great deal of.
equipment 是不可數名詞，後面的 most of it 也把它當成單數。所以數量詞要能接不可數名詞：a great deal of。

gloss.ex: The laboratory equipment arrived on Tuesday.
A technician installed the new printer.

point: both + A + and + B.
both A and B：both 搭配 and。
why: Both always pairs with and. Here it joins two descriptions of the chairs: both comfortable and easy to adjust.
both 一定搭配 and。這裡 and 連接兩個描述椅子的形容詞：both comfortable and easy to adjust。

gloss.ex: We asked customers for feedback.
You can adjust the height of the desk.

point: neither pairs with nor.
neither 搭配 nor。
why: Nor explained is the second half of a pair. The first half is neither approved. The and in sales and marketing only joins two departments.
nor explained 是成對句型的後半；前半就是 neither approved。sales and marketing 的 and 只是連接兩個部門。

gloss.ex: The regional director visits each office yearly.
Send your budget request to finance.
The hiring plan is on hold.

point: Joined by and, both verbs take the same form.
and 連接的兩個動詞，形式要相同。
why: And joins register and the blank. Both verbs follow must, so both are base forms: register … and keep. The phrase within 30 days of purchase just sits between them.
and 連接 register 和空格，兩個動詞都接在 must 後面，所以都用原形：register … and keep。within 30 days of purchase 只是插在中間。

gloss.ex: An extended warranty covers repairs for five years.
Please register your product online.
Keep the receipt as proof of purchase.

point: request that + subject + base verb.
request that + 主詞 + 原形動詞。
why: Requested that asks for an action, so the verb in the that clause is the base form. Each department head is singular, but the verb stays submit.
requested that 表示要求，that 子句的動詞用原形。each department head 雖是單數，動詞仍是 submit。

gloss.ex: The finance director approved the plan.
Each department head attends the weekly meeting.
Please read the revised schedule.

point: essential that + base verb; put not before it.
essential that + 原形動詞；否定把 not 放前面。
why: It is essential that asks for something, so the verb is a base form. To make it negative, put not before it. The draft agreement is the thing shared, so the verb is passive: not be shared.
It is essential that 表示必要，動詞用原形；否定就在前面加 not。草案是被分享的，所以用被動：not be shared。

gloss.ex: Please review the draft agreement today.
Clear signs are essential in a large building.

point: Had + subject + past participle = if … had.
Had + 主詞 + p.p. = if … had。
why: We would have found shows an imagined past. The matching if clause is if the supplier had notified us. Drop if and put had first: Had the supplier notified us.
we would have found 表示與過去事實相反。對應的 if 子句是 if the supplier had notified us；省略 if、把 had 放前面：Had the supplier notified us。

gloss.ex: Our supplier ships every Monday.
Please notify us of any changes.
We chose a new vendor for office supplies.
The parts arrived in time for the launch.

point: Not until + clause, then did + subject + base verb.
Not until + 子句，後面接 did + 主詞 + 原形動詞。
why: The sentence starts with Not until, so the main clause flips its order. The event is in the past and the verb is begin, a base form: did the error rate … begin.
句子以 Not until 開頭，主句要倒裝。事情發生在過去，動詞又是原形 begin：did the error rate … begin。

gloss.ex: We count our inventory every month.
The error rate dropped last quarter.
The warehouse is near the airport.

point: Remove it believes, then see what is missing.
先拿掉 it believes，再看缺什麼。
why: Take out it believes: the three candidates … are best qualified. The blank is the subject of are, and the candidates are people, so it is who.
拿掉 it believes 後是 the three candidates … are best qualified。空格是 are 的主詞，先行詞是人，所以用 who。

gloss.ex: The hiring committee meets on Thursday.
We interviewed five candidates this week.
She is qualified for the manager role.
The distribution center ships orders daily.

point: each of + plural noun: the verb is singular.
each of + 複數名詞：動詞用單數。
why: The subject is Each, not offices or the three. Including … last year is extra information. Each is singular, so the passive uses is required.
主詞是 Each，不是 offices 或 the three；including … last year 只是補充。each 是單數，被動用 is required。

gloss.ex: Everyone, including interns, must attend.
We publish a quarterly report.
Send the forms to the head office.

point: fewer + plural countable noun.
fewer + 可數複數名詞。
why: Than needs a comparative. The main noun is errors, which you can count, and shipping and billing only describe it. So the word is fewer.
有 than 要用比較級。中心名詞是可數的 errors，shipping and billing 只是修飾它，所以用 fewer。

gloss.ex: Barcode scanning speeds up our checkout.
A billing error delayed the payment.
Staff report any problems to the manager.

point: recommend that + subject + base verb.
recommend that + 主詞 + 原形動詞。
why: Recommended … that opens a clause with its own subject, the accounts payable team. A recommended action takes the base form, even with a singular subject: check.
recommended … that 後面是有自己主詞的子句，主詞是 the accounts payable team。建議的內容用原形，即使主詞是單數：check。

gloss.ex: In light of the delay, we changed plans.
The external auditors visit every spring.
The accounts payable team pays all bills.
Please send the invoice by email.

point: multiple + as + adjective + as.
倍數 + as + 形容詞 + as。
why: Powerful as the model follows the blank, so the pattern is as … as. A multiple like twice goes before the first as: twice as powerful as.
空格後面是 powerful as the model，句型是 as … as。twice 這類倍數放在第一個 as 前面：twice as powerful as。

gloss.ex: The vacuum cleaner is in the closet.
The box weighs five kilograms.
The new model replaces the old one.

point: contribute to: to is a preposition, so use -ing.
contribute to 的 to 是介系詞，後面接 -ing。
why: Contributed … to uses to as a preposition, even with significantly between them. A verb after it takes -ing: to reducing the time.
contributed … to 的 to 是介系詞，中間隔了 significantly 也一樣。後面的動詞用 -ing：to reducing the time。

gloss.ex: Two sorting machines handle all the parcels.
Better training contributed to our success.
Sales rose significantly last quarter.
Customer returns are checked on arrival.

point: those who + plural verb: the people who.
those who + 複數動詞：……的那些人。
why: The main verb is are entitled, so the subject is plural. Those who registered means 'the people who registered': Those.
主要動詞是 are entitled，所以主詞要是複數。Those who registered 是「報名的那些人」：Those。

gloss.ex: Over fifty people registered for the course.
The early deadline is next Friday.
Members will be entitled to a discount.

point: Should + subject + base verb = If … should.
Should + 主詞 + 原形 = If … should。
why: If you should have any questions drops if and puts should first: Should you have any questions. It is a polite way to say 'if you have questions' before please contact.
If you should have any questions 省略 if、把 should 放前面：Should you have any questions。是信件裡禮貌的「如果有疑問」，後面接 please contact。

gloss.ex: Customer service answers calls all day.
The store is closed on weekdays.
